Visit note | 2025-02-16 11:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Zakia Sarkar, 23, female. Miss Sarkar attends today reporting painful cramps during the first days of each period that sometimes cause her to miss work or classes, along with associated nausea. She works as a sales representative and mentions these symptoms have become worse since a stressful family move to Banani. She reports no other systemic issues or unusual bleeding patterns. On examination, her vital signs are: pain score 6/10, BP 122/85 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 67 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild tenderness in the lower abdomen without guarding or rigidity. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was advised to use a hot water bottle for comfort, engage in light exercise as tolerated, and keep a detailed period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.
